newsitem.title: MOROCCO: ONA group net profit rose to $93.4 mln/96.
newsitem.headline: ONA group net profit rose to $93.4 mln/96.

text.p: Morocco's largest private conglomerate and stock market blue chip ONA Group showed in its audited consolidated results a net profit of 878.7 million ($93.4 million) in 1996, up 45.8 percent from 1995.
"Despite a less favourable economic context in 1996, ONA group improved its profitability and posted a very positive results," ONA president Fouad Filali told a news conference.
Net profit rose to 878.7 million dirhams in 1996 from 602.6 million dirhams in the previous year, Filali said.
The group's consolidated turnover eased to 18.11 billion dirhams in 1996 from 18.57 billion dirhams in 1995, he said.
"The group continued to concentrate its efforts on the profitability issue...This is why the turnover nearly stagnated last year," Filali said.

The results, which were audited by U.S. Ernest and Young and Price Waterhouse institutions, showed the ONA continuing strategy with a focus on the core business including international, finance, mining and agro-industry sectors," he said.

ONA's four listed subsidiaries Edible oil firm Lesieur Cristal, sugar refinery Cosumar, agro- industry Centrale Laitiere, and Financiere Diwan showed a rise in net profits at between 344.6 million dirhams and 89.5 million dirhams in 1996 or an improvement of 161.5 percent, Gilles Denisty, chief operating officer, said.
The group disclosed the launch of a new sugar refinery "worth hundreds of millions dirhams" located in the same area of the Casablanca-based Cosumar refinery, an ONA manager said.
"The new refinery, which will provide the domestic market with a better quality sugar products, is expected to be operational in June 1997," the manager added.
He declined to give further details.

Morocco's main refinery and sugar importer, Cosumar refines an average 2,000 tonnes of raw sugar per day, a trader said. It imported more than 500,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1996 or nearly 50 percent of the country's consumption, he said.

ONA has reduced its debt to 1.7 billion dirhams in 1996 from to 2.3 billion dirhams, the group results showed. "To be noticed the 1.7 billion dirhams debt has no impact on our business if we take into account a sum of 1.5 billion dirhams which the state-owned Caisse de Compensation fund owes to ONA as arrears," the conglomerate said.
According to Filali, the group will pay a dividend of 15 dirhams to its shareholders, up from 14 dirhams in 1995 and 13 dirhams in 1994.
Filali said he was "optimistic for the group's business in 1997" but declined to give any figures.
The group expects to expand its mining activity and investments estimated at up to 100 million dirhams per year, Filali said.
"ONA's consolidated mining turnover rose 5.8 percent to 1.05 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with the previous year," he added.
Established in Casablanca in 1919, ONA is the first largest market capitalisation with 14.8 billion dirhams.
Among the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, ONA was last traded at 865 dirhams, a broker said.
